---
title: "What it does"
description: >-
  Every shortcut, what each one previews, and how the contact sheet, the EPUB conversion and the annotations work from a reader's side.
---

## Shortcuts

Every action has exactly one shortcut, and every one of them is
[configurable](settings.qmd).

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| **Space** | Preview the selected item's attachment. Again, or **Escape**, to dismiss. |
| **Shift+Space** | Preview the item's notes, rendered as a page. |
| **Ctrl+Shift+Space** | Contact sheet: every page of a PDF as a thumbnail. |
| **Ctrl+Alt+Space** | The same sheet in a Zotero window, which stays open beside the reader. |

The same actions sit in the right-click menu. The contact sheet entries appear
only when the selection actually contains a PDF.

The defaults are the same on every system; only the way they are written
differs, since ⌃⇧ are macOS keycaps and mean nothing elsewhere. They avoid the
combinations the systems take for themselves — Spotlight, input-source
switching, and the window menu a window manager claims before the application
is ever asked. There is more on that in [Architecture](dev/architecture.qmd).

Space is ignored while the item list is collecting a find-as-you-type search, so
typing a title with spaces in it still searches.

## What it previews

Anything the system's preview panel can show: PDFs, images, video, HTML, plain
text, office documents, and whatever a third-party preview extension adds. The
plugin hands the file over untouched.

**EPUB is the exception.** No system preview renders one, so zotLook converts
the book on the fly into a single styled page: the spine walked in reading
order, each chapter's body appended, the book's own stylesheets pulled in so its
layout and typography survive, and a Palatino base font in a book-width column
laid over the top. Images, fonts and inline SVGs resolve, because relative URLs
in both markup and CSS are rewritten. A converted book is cached until the file
changes.

At the top sits a **table of contents** that folds away and whose entries jump
to the chapter — inside the system preview too, where JavaScript is disabled.
The titles and their nesting come from the navigation the book carries, so they
are the publisher's rather than guesses drawn from headings. A book with no
navigation gets no box.

Because the plugin cannot reliably tell whether you have an EPUB preview
extension installed, the conversion is a [setting](settings.qmd) rather than a
guess: turn it off and the book goes to the panel like any other file.

## The contact sheet

Every page of a PDF as a thumbnail in a scrollable grid — useful for finding the
figure you remember, or for seeing at a glance which pages you marked up.

- **Annotations are drawn in**, so the marked-up pages stand out.
- **Clicking a page opens it in Zotero's reader** at that page. This works from
  the preview panel on all three systems, and from the window variant.
- **The layout adapts.** A document with few pages gets fewer columns and
  correspondingly sharper thumbnails, so it fills the width instead of leaving
  space. The column count is configurable.
- **No page limit by default.** A 300-page book takes a few seconds. A limit can
  be set for unusually large scans; when it bites, the sheet says how many pages
  it is showing.

The window variant (**Ctrl+Alt+Space**) puts the same sheet in a Zotero window.
The difference is what happens after a click: the panel closes as it hands over
to the reader, the window stays open beside it.

## Which attachment gets previewed

Selecting a parent item previews **one** of its attachments. By default the
order is PDF, EPUB, HTML, image, video, anything else — and it is a ranking, not
a filter: a type near the bottom is still used when nothing above it is present.
You can [reorder it](settings.qmd), or switch to simply taking the first
attachment the item lists.

Only the chosen attachment is ever resolved. Resolving them all would download
every synced attachment of every selected item only to throw all but one away.

## Localisation

Menu entries, settings and progress messages are available in English and
German, following Zotero's own language setting.
